11.solution: The conjugate base is formed by removing one proton: \(\mathrm{NH_3} - \mathrm{H^+} = \mathrm{NH_2^-}\).

13.subtopic: Group 1 Alkali Metals, Properties and Reactivity
13.solution: Lithium nitrate behaves like Group 2 nitrates: \(4\mathrm{LiNO_3} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Li_2O} + 4\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathrm{O_2}\). The other alkali metal nitrates give the nitrite and \(\mathrm{O_2}\).

14.solution: FTIR records infrared absorption by functional groups, which tells the binding nature of molecules on the nanoparticles. UV-visible spectroscopy, XRD and SEM give the other three.

15.solution: Allyl bromide is \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2Br}\). Numbering from the double bond end puts Br on C-3: 3-bromopropene.

16.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
16.solution: Using the ash as a raw material turns a waste into a product, which is the principle of preventing waste.

17.solution: Polonium is simple cubic, so \(a = 2r = 380\) pm and the cell volume is \((3.8 \times 10^{-8})^3 = 5.487 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\). The voids are \(47.6\%\) of it: \(0.476 \times 5.487 \times 10^{-23} = 2.613 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).

19.subtopic: Unit Cells, Edge Length and Atomic Radius
19.solution: Six face centres, each shared by two cells: \(6 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 3\) atoms.

20.subtopic: Types of Solutions, Solubility and Henry's Law
20.solution: By Henry's law solubility is proportional to partial pressure: \(6.85 \times 10^{-4} \times 0.50 = 3.425 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}\).

22.subtopic: Van't Hoff Factor and Abnormal Molar Mass

23.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
23.solution: Ions migrating from the salt bridge balance the charge building up in each half-cell, keeping both electrically neutral so the current continues.

25.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
25.solution: \(E^0(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}/Fe}) = -0.44\) V is higher than \(E^0(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}/Zn}) = -0.76\) V, so zinc is oxidised as the anode and iron stays the cathode. Option C is wrong because zinc has the higher oxidation potential.

26.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
26.solution: Rate \(= k[A]^2\), so doubling \([A]\) multiplies the rate by \(2^2 = 4\).

27.subtopic: Reaction Mechanism, Intermediates and Rate-Determining Step
27.solution: The slow step gives \(r = k[\mathrm{NOBr_2}][\mathrm{NO}]\). The fast equilibrium gives \([\mathrm{NOBr_2}] = K[\mathrm{NO}][\mathrm{Br_2}]\), so \(r = k'[\mathrm{NO}]^2[\mathrm{Br_2}]\) with the intermediate removed.

28.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
28.solution: Two reactant molecules take part (bimolecular), and the order is the sum of the exponents: \(1 + \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

29.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
29.solution: By the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion rises with its charge, so \(\mathrm{Al^{3+}}\) is the most effective for a negative sol.

30.solution: The Haber process uses finely divided iron with molybdenum as the promoter.

31.solution: The central atom of an interhalogen is the larger, less electronegative halogen. Fluorine is the smallest and most electronegative, and it has no vacant d orbitals, so it is never central.

32.subtopic: Position, Electronic Configuration and General Features of d-Block
32.solution: Interstitial compounds form when small atoms such as H, C or N occupy the vacant spaces (interstices) in the crystal lattice of transition metals.

33.solution: In D a water molecule moves between the coordination sphere and the lattice: solvate (hydrate) isomers. A shows linkage, B ionisation and C coordination isomerism.

34.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
34.solution: \(\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\) is \(3d^6\). \(\mathrm{F^-}\) is a weak field ligand, so the 3d electrons stay unpaired and the outer 4s, 4p and 4d orbitals are used: \(sp^3d^2\) (high spin, outer orbital complex).

35.solution: Primary halides react by \(S_N2\) and tertiary by \(S_N1\). A secondary halide such as 2-bromopropane can follow either path.

36.subtopic: Polyhalogen Compounds — Freon, DDT, War Gases
36.solution: Direct contact of dichloromethane (methylene chloride) with the eyes can burn the cornea.

37.subtopic: Physical Properties of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
37.solution: Ethyl methyl ether (boiling point about \(281\) K) is a gas at room temperature. The aromatic ethers are liquids or solids.

38.solution: Ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid gives ethoxyethane at \(413\) K. At \(443\) K it gives ethene instead.

39.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
39.solution: Reaction with Na shows an OH group, and PCC oxidation to acetaldehyde \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\) shows a primary alcohol with two carbons: ethyl alcohol.

40.solution: Ethers and alcohols share the formula \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n+2}O}\), for example \(\mathrm{CH_3OCH_3}\) and \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\).

41.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
41.solution: Acid-catalysed dehydration acts on alcohols, and a tertiary alcohol dehydrates most readily. 2-Methylbutan-2-ol loses water to give the more substituted alkene, 2-methylbut-2-ene.

42.solution: Two acetone molecules give diacetone alcohol \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2COCH_3}\), which loses water to form \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C{=}CHCOCH_3}\), 4-methylpent-3-en-2-one.

43.solution: Schiff's reagent turns pink with aldehydes. Ketones, acids and esters do not restore the colour.

44.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
44.solution: Carboxylic acids liberate \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) with brisk effervescence from sodium bicarbonate. Tollen's and Fehling's test aldehydes, and \(\mathrm{NaHSO_3}\) adds to carbonyl compounds.

45.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
45.solution: Highest \(pK_b\) means weakest base. The \(-\mathrm{CF_3}\) group has the strongest \(-I\) effect and it is nearest to N in C, so that amine is the weakest base.

46.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
46.solution: Sucrose is a disaccharide of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose and \(\beta\)-D-fructose. Hydrolysis gives one molecule of each.

47.subtopic: Nucleic Acids, DNA, RNA, Nucleotides and Bases
47.solution: A nucleoside is a sugar and a base only. A ribonucleoside has D-ribose with a base such as cytosine; adding phosphate gives a nucleotide.

48.solution: Cholesterol and other lipids travel in the blood as lipoproteins (such as LDL and HDL).

49.solution: PHBV, poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate), is a copolymer of 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid.

50.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
50.solution: In a quaternary ammonium salt with a long alkyl chain the cation carries the hydrophobic tail, so these salts act as cationic detergents.

51.subtopic: Composite Functions — f∘g, Iteration and Functional Identities
51.solution: Replacing \(x\) by \(1 - x\): \(f(1 - x) + 2f(x) = (1 - x)^2 + 5\). Doubling this and subtracting the given equation: \(3f(x) = 2(1 - x)^2 + 10 - x^2 - 5 = x^2 - 4x + 7\), so \(f(x) = \dfrac{(x - 2)^2 + 3}{3}\).

53.solution: Squaring: \(1 + \sin 2x = \dfrac{1}{4}\), so \(\sin 2x = \dfrac{2t}{1 + t^2} = -\dfrac{3}{4}\) with \(t = \tan x\), i.e. \(3t^2 + 8t + 3 = 0\). Both roots give a genuine solution (one in each of the second and fourth quadrants), so the sum is \(-\dfrac{8}{3}\).

54.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
54.solution: The median \(BE^2 = \dfrac{2(BC^2) + 2(AB^2) - CA^2}{4} = \dfrac{98 + 162 - 64}{4} = 49\), so \(BE = 7\) m. Height \(= 7 \times 4 = 28\) m.

55.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
55.solution: Angles in A.P. make the middle angle \(60^\circ\), opposite the middle side \(9\). With third side \(x\): \(81 = 100 + x^2 - 10x\), so \(x^2 - 10x + 19 = 0\) and \(x = 5 \pm \sqrt{6}\) (both less than \(9\)).

56.subtopic: Algebra of Complex Numbers — Conjugates, Powers of i and Cube Roots of Unity

57.subtopic: Arrangements with Constraints — Together, Never Together, Fixed Positions and Repeated Letters
57.solution: Words starting with E: \(4! = 24\); with H: \(\dfrac{4!}{2!} = 12\) (36 so far); with R: \(12\) (48 so far). The 48th is the last R word, RTHEE, so the 47th is the one before it, RTEHE.

58.subtopic: Angle Between the Pair — Perpendicular Pairs, Lines at a Given Angle and the Bisectors
58.solution: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{|a + b|}\). First pair: \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{49/4 - 12}}{7} = \dfrac{1}{7}\). Second pair: \(\dfrac{2\sqrt{25/4 - 6}}{7} = \dfrac{1}{7}\). So \(\theta_1 = \theta_2\).

59.subtopic: Distance From a Point to a Circle — Greatest, Least, a Line Cutting the Circle and the Segment Area
59.solution: The nearest point lies on the ray from the centre \((0, 0)\) through \((2, 0)\), at distance \(2\sqrt{2}\): \((2\sqrt{2}, 0)\).

60.subtopic: Tangents — At a Point, With a Given Slope, From an External Point and Their Loci
60.solution: The circle is \(x^2 + y^2 - 4x + 2y + \dfrac{5}{2} = 0\): centre \((2, -1)\), \(r^2 = \dfrac{5}{2}\). Distance to the centre is \(\sqrt{5}\), so \(\sin\dfrac{\theta}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5/2}}{\sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).

61.subtopic: Slope, Angle Between Lines and Rotation

63.solution: The \(1^\infty\) form gives \(\lim_{x \to 0}\left(1 + \dfrac{f(x)}{x^2}\right) = 3\), so \(\dfrac{f(x)}{x^2} \to 2\) and \(f(x) = 2x^2\). By parts, \(\int 2x^2\log x\, dx = \dfrac{2x^3}{3}\log x - \dfrac{2x^3}{9} + c = \dfrac{2}{9}x^3(3\log x - 1) + c\).

64.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding f(c) and the Parameter
64.solution: \(1 - \cos 6x \approx 18x^2\), so the numerator \(\approx \dfrac{(18x^2)^2}{2} = 162x^4\). The denominator \(\approx 9x^4\), so \(f(0) = 18\).

65.solution: The right side is \(\lim \dfrac{n + 2}{n} = 1\). The numerator is \((k^x - 5^x)^2 \approx x^2\left(\ln\dfrac{k}{5}\right)^2\) and the denominator \(\approx 9x^2\), so \(\left(\ln\dfrac{k}{5}\right)^2 = 9\). With \(k > 5\), \(\ln\dfrac{k}{5} = 3\) and \(k = 5e^3\).

66.subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
66.solution: The three terms cover every case except \(p\) and \(q\) both true, so the statement is \(\sim(p \wedge q) \equiv \sim p \vee \sim q\).

67.solution: For \(x = 1\), \(x^2 - x = 0\), so \(p\) is false. \(x = 10 \in A\) satisfies \(x + 10 = 20\), so \(q\) is true.

68.subtopic: Finding Truth Values of Component Statements
68.solution: A false implication needs \(p \wedge \sim q\) true and \(q \vee \sim r\) false: \(p = T\), \(q = F\), \(r = T\). Then B is \(F \rightarrow T\), which is true; A, C and D are all false.

70.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Identities — Sums, Substitution and Telescoping
70.solution: Put \(x = \tan\theta\) with \(0 \le \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{4}\). Both inverse functions equal \(2\theta\), so the bracket is \(\theta + \theta = 2\theta\) and \(\tan 2\theta = \dfrac{2x}{1 - x^2}\).

71.subtopic: Inverse of a Matrix — Adjoint Formula, Products and Verification

72.subtopic: Inverse of a Matrix — Adjoint Formula, Products and Verification
72.solution: From \(AA^{-1} = I\): row 1 of \(A\) times column 3 gives \(0 + c + 1 = 0\), so \(c = -1\). Row 3 times column 1 gives \(\dfrac{3}{2} - 4a + \dfrac{5}{2} = 0\), so \(a = 1\).

73.subtopic: Systems of Linear Equations and Symmetric, Skew-Symmetric Matrices
73.solution: A common line needs a non-trivial solution: \(\begin{vmatrix} a & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & b & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & c \end{vmatrix} = abc - a - b - c - 2 = 0\). So \(a + b + c - abc = -2\).

74.subtopic: Derivative of One Function with Respect to Another
74.solution: \(\dfrac{f'(\sin x)\cos x}{-g'(\cos x)\sin x}\) at \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3} \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{-(-2) \cdot \frac{1}{2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

76.solution: With \(t = x - 1\), \(f = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(t + \dfrac{t^3}{3} + \dfrac{t^5}{5} + \ldots\right) = \dfrac{1}{8}\log\dfrac{1 + t}{1 - t} = \dfrac{1}{8}\log\dfrac{x}{2 - x}\). So \(f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{8}\left(\dfrac{1}{x} + \dfrac{1}{2 - x}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4x(2 - x)}\).

77.subtopic: Tangents, Normals, and the Slope of a Curve
77.solution: A vertical normal means a horizontal tangent: \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{2} = 0\) at \(x = 1\), where \(y = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 1\).

78.subtopic: Rate of Change and Related Rates
78.solution: With \(h = 2r\), \(V = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi r^3\) and \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 2\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}\). So \(-12\pi = 8\pi\dfrac{dr}{dt}\) and \(\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -1.5\) cm/sec: decreasing at \(1.5\) cm/sec.

79.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms
79.solution: The standard result is \(\sqrt{2}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\tan x - 1}{\sqrt{2\tan x}}\right) + c\), so \(a = \sqrt{2}\), \(b = 2\) and \(a^{10} + b^5 = 32 + 32 = 64\).

80.solution: For \(|3x| < 1\) the integrand is \(2\tan^{-1}3x\). By parts: \(2x\tan^{-1}3x - \int\dfrac{6x}{1 + 9x^2}dx = 2x\tan^{-1}3x - \dfrac{1}{3}\log(1 + 9x^2) + c\).

82.subtopic: King's Property — f(a + b − x) and the f/(f + g) Family
82.solution: The limits add to \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), so replacing \(x\) by \(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x\) turns \(\tan\) into \(\cot\). Adding the two forms: \(2I = \dfrac{3\pi}{10} - \dfrac{\pi}{5} = \dfrac{\pi}{10}\), so \(I = \dfrac{\pi}{20}\).

83.subtopic: Evaluating Definite Integrals — Standard Forms, Algebraic Substitution and By Parts
83.solution: Put \(x = \dfrac{1}{t}\): \(dx = -\dfrac{dt}{t^2}\) and the limits swap, giving \(I = \int_{1/2}^{2}\dfrac{1}{t}\sin^{101}\left(\dfrac{1}{t} - t\right)dt = -I\). So \(I = 0\).

85.subtopic: Area Under a Curve — Between a Curve and an Axis
85.solution: The curve meets the axis at \(x = 0\) and \(x = 4\): \(\int_0^4(4x - x^2)dx = 32 - \dfrac{64}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}\).

86.solution: Regroup as \(\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)(y\,dx - x\,dy) + y\,dy = 0\) and divide by \(y^2\): \(\sec^2\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)d\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) + \dfrac{dy}{y} = 0\). Integrating, \(\tan\dfrac{x}{y} + \log|y| = c\).

87.solution: \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{y}{x + 1} = e^x(x + 1)\), with integrating factor \(\dfrac{1}{x + 1}\). Then \(\dfrac{y}{x + 1} = \int e^x dx = e^x + c\), so \(y = (x + 1)(e^x + c)\).

90.solution: Write \(\bar{c} = \lambda\bar{a} + \mu\bar{b}\). Then \(\bar{c} \cdot \bar{a} = 6\lambda - 2\mu = 0\), so \(\mu = 3\lambda\) and \(\bar{c} = \lambda(5\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} - 5\hat{k})\). The modulus condition gives two values \(\lambda = \pm\sqrt{3/5}\), so the two values of \(y = 5\lambda\) add to \(0\).

91.solution: Let \(\bar{u} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, m, n\right)\). \(|\bar{u} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}|^2 = 1 + 2(m + n) + 2 = 1\) gives \(m + n = -1\). The sum of projections is \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - 1\).

92.subtopic: Vector Geometry — Section Formula, Triangle, and Parallelogram
92.solution: \(AB = |(1, 2, 1)| = \sqrt{6}\) and \(AC = |(-6, 3, -3)| = 3\sqrt{6}\), so \(BD : DC = 1 : 3\) and \(D = \dfrac{3B + C}{4} = \left(\dfrac{1}{4}, \dfrac{5}{4}, -3\right)\). Then \(\overrightarrow{AD} = \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}, \dfrac{9}{4}, 0\right)\) and \(AD = \dfrac{3}{4}\sqrt{10}\).

94.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
94.solution: \(y\) is fixed at \(-\dfrac{2}{3}\) along the line, so the line has no \(y\) component: \(m = 0\). (Its direction is \(\left(\dfrac{3}{2}, 0, \dfrac{1}{3}\right) \propto (9, 0, 2)\).)

95.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
95.solution: \(\dfrac{1}{a} = \dfrac{-1}{b} = \dfrac{-1}{c}\), so the direction is along \((1, -1, -1)\). Taking the sense with a positive \(z\) component, \((-1, 1, 1)\), gives \(\cos\gamma = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

96.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
96.solution: Squaring \(l + m + n = 1\) gives \(lm + mn + nl = 0\). With all three non-negative, at most one of them is non-zero, so one cosine is \(1\) and the others \(0\): the vector lies along an axis.

97.subtopic: Formulation and Special Cases — Word Problems and Infinitely Many Optima
97.solution: The objective is parallel to the binding constraint \(x + y = 150\), which forms an edge of the feasible region from \((150, 0)\) to \((100, 50)\). Every point of that edge gives \(Z = 150\), so there are infinitely many optima.

104.solution: \(r = 40\) m. Distance \(= \dfrac{3}{4} \times 2\pi \times 40 = 60\pi\) m. Three quarters of a turn ends \(90^\circ\) from the start, so displacement \(= r\sqrt{2} = 40\sqrt{2}\) m.

105.subtopic: Newton's Laws — Force, Tension, Lift, and Connected Blocks
105.solution: \(F = \dfrac{k}{v}\) makes the power \(Fv = k\) constant, so \(\dfrac{d(KE)}{dt} = k\) and the kinetic energy grows linearly with time.

106.subtopic: Elasticity, Springs, and Energy in Strained Solids

107.subtopic: Rotational Kinetic Energy and Rolling Motion
107.solution: \(v^2 = \dfrac{2gh}{1 + K^2/R^2}\): ring \(v^2 = gh\), sphere \(v^2 = \dfrac{10gh}{7}\). Ratio \(= \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{10}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3.5}{5}}\), so \(x = 3.5\).

109.subtopic: Gravitational PE, Escape Velocity, and Energy
109.solution: \(\dfrac{1}{2}mK^2\dfrac{2GM}{R} = \dfrac{GMm}{R} - \dfrac{GMm}{R + h}\) gives \(\dfrac{R}{R + h} = 1 - K^2\), so \(h = \dfrac{RK^2}{1 - K^2}\).

110.solution: \(h = \dfrac{2T\cos\theta}{r\rho g}\) varies as \(\dfrac{1}{g}\), so the rise on the moon is \(6\) times larger.

111.subtopic: Viscosity, Stokes' Law, Terminal Velocity, and Reynolds
111.solution: At terminal velocity, viscous force \(=\) weight \(-\) buoyancy \(= Mg - \dfrac{M}{d} \cdot \dfrac{d}{2}g = \dfrac{Mg}{2}\).

112.solution: Volume is conserved, so \(R = 2^{1/3}r\). Energy released \(= T(2 \cdot 4\pi r^2 - 4\pi R^2) = 4\pi r^2T(2 - 2^{2/3})\).

113.solution: The temperature rise is \(\dfrac{\Delta Q}{ms}\) and the areal coefficient is \(2\alpha\), so \(\Delta A = A(2\alpha)\dfrac{\Delta Q}{ms}\).

114.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
114.solution: \(P = \dfrac{\mathrm{constant}}{V}\) is isothermal, so \(T\) stays constant while \(P\) falls from state 1 to state 2. On a \(T\)-\(p\) diagram this is a horizontal line with 1 at the higher pressure (right) and 2 at the lower: diagram (c).

115.subtopic: First Law, Internal Energy, and Work-Heat Relations
115.solution: \(\Delta U = Q - \dfrac{Q}{4} = \dfrac{3Q}{4}\) and \(\Delta U = 2 \cdot \dfrac{5}{2}R\,\Delta T = 5R\,\Delta T\). So \(Q = \dfrac{20R}{3}\Delta T\) and the heat capacity is \(\dfrac{20R}{3}\).

116.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
116.solution: No heat is exchanged (\(dQ = 0\)) while the temperature changes, so \(C = \dfrac{dQ}{n\,dT} = 0\).

119.solution: Momentum is conserved at the mean position: \(v_2 = \dfrac{v_1}{2}\). Also \(\omega_2 = \dfrac{\omega_1}{\sqrt{2}}\). From \(A_2\omega_2 = \dfrac{A_1\omega_1}{2}\): \(A_2 = \dfrac{A_1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\dfrac{A_1}{A_2} = \sqrt{2}\).

120.solution: Angular acceleration \(= \dfrac{g}{\ell}\theta\). Equal values give \(\dfrac{\theta_1}{\ell_1} = \dfrac{\theta_2}{\ell_2}\), i.e. \(\theta_1\ell_2 = \theta_2\ell_1\).

121.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
121.solution: Particle speeds are always equal when the phase difference is \(\pi\) (velocities equal and opposite), and the least such separation is \(\dfrac{\lambda}{2}\).

122.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
122.solution: Closed pipe, first overtone: \(\dfrac{3v}{4L_1}\). Open pipe, third overtone: \(\dfrac{4v}{2L_2}\). Equating, \(\dfrac{L_1}{L_2} = \dfrac{3}{8}\).

123.subtopic: Pipes, Resonance Tube, and Doppler Effect
123.solution: The air column becomes \(\dfrac{4L}{5}\), and \(n = \dfrac{v}{4L}\) varies as \(\dfrac{1}{L}\), so the frequency becomes \(\dfrac{5}{4}\) times: an increase of \(25\%\).

124.subtopic: Progressive Wave, Wave Equation, and Velocity
124.solution: \(60^\circ\) is \(\dfrac{1}{6}\) of a cycle, so \(\lambda = 6 \times 6 = 36\) cm and \(v = 500 \times 0.36 = 180\) m/s.

125.solution: Each shell contributes \(\dfrac{q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 a} = \dfrac{\sigma 4\pi a^2}{4\pi\epsilon_0 a} = \dfrac{\sigma a}{\epsilon_0}\) at the centre, so \(V = \dfrac{\sigma(R + r)}{\epsilon_0}\).

127.solution: The first and fourth capacitors each join A to B, so they are in parallel. The middle two run in series from one A junction to the other, so both their ends are at A and they carry no charge. \(C_{AB} = 16 + 16 = 32\ \mu F\).

130.solution: The three cells are in series the same way round: e.m.f. \(6\) V, internal resistance \(3\,\Omega\). \(I = \dfrac{6}{3 + 2} = 1.2\) A.

131.solution: \(B = \mu nI\) does not depend on the radius or area and falls with lower current; a core of higher permeability \(\mu\) increases it.

134.solution: \(M = \dfrac{10^{-3}}{3}\) H is the same both ways, so the flux through \(P\) is \(M \times 2 = 0.667 \times 10^{-3}\) Wb.

137.solution: \(120\) V is the rms value, so \(V_0 = 120\sqrt{2} = 169.7\) V. \(\omega t = 2\pi \times 60 \times \dfrac{1}{720} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\), so \(V = 169.7 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 84.8\) V.
